title: Az étteremben: Ordering and Eating Out

sections.title: Eating what you cooked, or eating out
sections.content: The same food vocabulary works whether you're cooking at home or ordering in a restaurant. szeretnék (Unit 16's polite "I would like") is exactly how you order, and the past tense from Units 24-25 tells the story afterwards.

items.spanish: Az étteremben a pincértől kértünk egy asztalt az ablak mellett.
items.english: At the restaurant we asked the waiter for a table by the window.
I'd like to order soup and goulash.

items.spanish: A vacsora végén elkértük a számlát, és kártyával fizettünk.
items.english: At the end of dinner we asked for the bill, and paid by card.

sections.content: Szeretnék rendelni is polite and general ("I'd like to order"); once you know exactly what you want, just name it — Egy levest és egy gulyást kérek — kérek works just as well as szeretnék for ordering food.
